description: QuipMac is a NATIVE macOS SwiftUI app — NOT a web app. This PRD extends the Windows-list sidebar's magic-wand button in QuipMac/Views/WindowListSidebar.swift. Today a wand tap ONLY sorts the windows (terminals on top, attention-needed first; simulators next; everything else below) by writing a new order to the `windowOrder` binding via magicSort(). This PRD makes the SAME single tap ALSO toggle the enabled-state (the row checkbox) of the dev windows — terminals (tier 0) and simulators (tier 1) — so one tap sorts them to the top AND turns them on, and the next tap turns them off. HARD CONSTRAINTS (do not violate): (1) Edit ONLY QuipMac/Views/WindowListSidebar.swift for code. (2) Verify each story ONLY by running `xcodebuild build -project QuipMac/QuipMac.xcodeproj -scheme QuipMac -destination 'platform=macOS,name=My Mac' -derivedDataPath build` and confirming the output contains '** BUILD SUCCEEDED **'. SourceKit / IDE 'Cannot find type X in scope' (WindowManager, ManagedWindow, TerminalApp, TerminalStateDetector) or 'Generic parameter T could not be inferred' errors are SPURIOUS cross-file noise — xcodebuild is the ONLY compile oracle; ignore IDE diagnostics. (3) Do NOT install to /Applications, do NOT run ditto / killall / codesign / open, do NOT touch TCC, do NOT use the dev-browser skill or any browser (this is a native macOS app, there is no web surface). A human installs and visually verifies separately. (4) Preserve ALL existing behavior verbatim: the sort logic in magicSort() (tier order, attention-first for terminals, subtitle tiebreak, offset stability), the native .onMove drag-reorder (dragReorder), the per-row hover chevrons (moveWindow/moveAction), syncWindowOrder, and orderedWindows. ADD the enable-toggle and tooltip text only — do NOT change the sort order, the drag, or the chevrons. (5) Match existing patterns in the file: classify targets with the existing windowTier(_:) helper (tier 0 = terminals, tier 1 = simulators); change enabled-state ONLY through windowManager.toggleWindow(id, enabled:) (the same path the row checkbox and the phone use — never a private/local @State mirror); keep the wand action wrapped in the existing withAnimation(.easeOut(duration: 0.22)) envelope so sort + checkbox flips read as one motion. (6) Stay on eb-branch; never push; never git add -A — add only the changed file(s) plus prd.json and progress.txt.

userStories.title: Wand tap toggles enable-state of terminals + simulators
userStories.description: As a developer, I want one tap of the magic wand to both sort my dev windows to the top AND turn them on (checked), so I don't have to sort and then tick each checkbox by hand. A second tap turns them off.
acceptanceCriteria: A wand tap still sorts the list exactly as today (terminals -> attention-first -> simulators -> rest). The existing sort logic in magicSort() is unchanged.

In the SAME tap, the enabled-state of all TARGET windows (windowTier(window) <= 1, i.e. tier 0 terminals + tier 1 simulators) is toggled: if EVERY target is currently enabled -> set all targets disabled; if ANY target is currently disabled -> set ALL targets enabled.
Tier-2 ('everything else') windows are NEVER enabled or disabled by the wand.
Enable/disable goes through windowManager.toggleWindow(id, enabled:) — not a private/local @State mirror.
When there are NO target windows, the tap still sorts and does not crash or toggle anything.
Sort + checkbox flips are wrapped in the existing withAnimation envelope so they read as one motion.
userStories.notes: Extended magicSort() in WindowListSidebar.swift: after building the sorted id list, compute targets = windows.filter { windowTier($0) <= 1 }, allOn = !targets.isEmpty && allSatisfy isEnabled, enableAll = !allOn, then inside the existing withAnimation(.easeOut(0.22)) loop windowManager.toggleWindow(target.id, enabled: enableAll) for each target. Sort logic byte-for-byte unchanged; empty targets skip the loop (no crash, still sorts). xcodebuild BUILD SUCCEEDED.

userStories.title: Wand tooltip reflects the new enable behavior
userStories.description: As a user, I want the wand's tooltip to tell me it also enables/disables my dev windows so the toggle isn't a surprise.
acceptanceCriteria: The wand button .help(...) tooltip names BOTH actions — auto-sort AND toggle-enable terminals + simulators (e.g. 'Auto-sort + toggle your dev windows — terminals and simulators to the top and enabled; tap again to turn them off').
No other behavior changes: drag-reorder, chevrons, and the add/refresh buttons are untouched.
